title: The Line Between Slave and Master
text: And so, I too performed a routine with Wolf as my partner. I fought the wolf as it leapt at me from every direction with flashy flourishes, subduing it as easily as twisting a newborn babe. The audience broke into pattering applause, I say. And by the time the very first circus program had run its full course, the crowd seemed thoroughly satisfied, looking quite delighted indeed. The human staff, Father included, came out onto the stage, raised both hands, and bowed to close the show. Once every last customer had filed out of the tent, Father let the curtain fall and exhaled, looking relieved.
“Alright, everyone, good work! The show went well. You all did great.”
“We did it, I say!”
“Yaaay!”
“Circus!”
“It’s a carnival!”
“It’s dark dance theater!”
Filolial-sama and I raised our voices in high spirits, following Father’s words.
“Kweh!”
“Kweh!”
Yuki-chan and the others who’d taken part in the program let out cheerful cries as well. Before long, they’d surely take on their angelic forms.
“Everyone did wonderfully.”
Elephant praised Filolial-sama and the others too.
“It makes me want to put together an even flashier program. I held back since it was our first show, but now I want to put more effort into it.”
“Elmelo-san seems to have a real knack for this sort of thing.”
“I—I wouldn’t say that much…”
“Elephant is quite skilled, indeed. Skilled enough to give Filolial-sama singing lessons in the end, I’d wager.”
“It’d be nice to work Elmelo-san’s singing into a program somewhere. If possible, I’d like to do away with the freak-show business altogether.”
Father said this while looking, with heartfelt distaste, at the mixed-breed Lizardman and Rabbit Man who were joining in the applause. The slaves gave a wry laugh.

“The earnings were decent enough. Customer satisfaction was good, so I expect even more people tomorrow. I heard folks saying they’d thought it was just a cheap freak show, but it turned out to be affordable and full of things worth seeing, and that they’d come again tomorrow.”
The Siltvelt envoy said this while checking over the ledger.
“I figured the first show wouldn’t draw much of a crowd, but word of mouth should build things up from here, so let’s keep at it without losing heart.”
According to Father, the circus wasn’t his real business, just a front—so in truth, whether it sold well or not didn’t matter to him. But even so, it seemed making it fun for everyone still mattered.
“Well then, as a reward, I’ll cook everyone a meal, so look forward to it.”
“Ohhh!”
“Now then, cleanup duty, if you please!”
“Wow!”

And so, while helping with the cleanup, Father cooked and raised everyone’s spirits along the way, I say. Then, once everyone had settled down to sleep… guided by the slave trader’s subordinates and the Siltvelt envoy, Father seemed to be heading out to a noble’s residence in town for some slave trading business.
“Well, I’m off then.”
“Safe travels, I say.”
“…Don’t make too friendly a face out there, or they’ll walk all over you.”
“Do take care.”
“Kuun…”
Besides me, the mixed-breed Lizardman, the Rabbit Man, and Wolf all saw Father off.
“Hey now… why is it that Shion and the rest keep fussing over me like a bunch of guardians? I know how to carry myself in situations like this.”

Indeed, when it came to business dealings, Father could act his part flawlessly. Putting on an utterly convincing performance to haggle prices down was one of Father’s true specialties, I say. Still, he grumbled that everyone had simply gotten too used to him by now. Incidentally, Filolial-sama and the others were sleeping however they pleased behind the circus tent. Around the time the circus ended, it seemed the town’s children had come around back to see Filolial-sama and the others.
“In the first place, Theodore, it’s because your acting was so over the top that someone actually wanted to buy you. Turning them down wasn’t easy at all, you know. Or would you rather be taken in?”
“…Th-that, please spare me. I’ll work on toning down the acting.”

It seemed a noble had requested to torture the Rabbit Man specifically. So this was how slave trading sometimes came about. Father said he wouldn’t sell him, of course. As for the negotiations to smooth things over instead, the monster trader’s subordinates seemed to be arranging something.
“Well, I do plan to talk my way into selling them some other merchandise instead. This time it’s… more like an apology visit, so Raphtalia-chan and the others don’t need to come along, but…”

I suddenly recalled how the monster trader had seemed to find Father’s negotiation tactics rather entertaining. The subordinates had even prepared a recording crystal for their report. I wasn’t quite sure what exactly got sold, but the negotiations seemed to be going well.
“Selling off a slave you’ve trained up… huh. Being a slave trader must be tough work in all sorts of ways. If I could, I’d rather just do the circus and skip the slave trading altogether.”
Father gave a wry laugh, saying that doing the circus together with everyone was genuinely fun.
“Well… no, never mind. Don’t worry about it.”
“—It’s not self-satisfaction. I’ve been thinking that too, these past few days, from how things have gone.”
“Indeed. I don’t feel bad about it either.”

The Rabbit Man and the mixed-breed Lizardman finished the sentence Father had swallowed back. Father had once said, with a self-deprecating air, that no matter how close a slave and master might grow, there was always a line drawn somewhere—that even with all the closeness in the world, there were stories of masters murdered the very next day. This seemed to be something every version of Father shared in common, one way or another. By nature, Father was a kind man, indeed. Keeping slaves in service must have weighed on him as a burden. And yet, the slaves themselves seemed to sense that worry of his.
“Father, let’s set aside the gloomy talk for now—there’s something I’d like you to see before you head out, I say!”
“What is it, Motoyasu-kun?”
“Yuki-chan and Kou!”
“Kweh?”

I called out to Yuki-chan and the others, who had already grown remarkably in a short span of time. They’d been resting behind the tent, but they came at my call. Elephant, who’d been tending to Kou, came along as well.
“Those little ones grew so big in such a short time.”
“Elmelo-san came too, I see.”
“Yes.”
“Filolial-sama, I believe it’s about time you take on angelic forms, just as the other angels have. Do show us that form, I say!”

At my words, Yuki-chan and the others began to transform. And then Yuki-chan and Kou took on the youthful forms I recognized so well. There had been a chance Yuki-chan might take on an adult form instead, but it seemed there was no trouble on that front.
“Motoyasu-sama~”
“Yaaay.”
“Thank you for showing us your angelic forms, I say!”
I’d need to prepare clothes for them after this, of course.
“Wow, Yuki-chan and the others turned into angels too.”
By now, everyone at the circus was so used to the sight of Filolial-sama’s forms that no one so much as blinked.
“What do you think? Elmelo?”
“So you can take human form too.”
“Mm-hm.”
Incidentally, before I’d called them over, Kou had apparently been chatting a bit with Elephant. But almost immediately, Kou puffed back into Filolial-sama’s regular form with a poof.
“How was it, Motoyasu-sama? Did Yuki manage to look properly like a leader?”
“Perfectly so, I say.”
“Thank you very much! Then Yuki shall go teach the rest of the Filolials just who is the leader of this flock!”
“Just don’t put too much tension in your shoulders about it, alright? It could backfire on you.”
“Of course.”

Yuki-chan nodded at Father’s warning. Incidentally, during the tag games at the midday break, Yuki-chan had already been showing off just how fast she could run. The other Filolial-sama still saw her as a promising newcomer, but they seemed to be gradually placing their trust in her. Before long, no doubt, everyone would come to rely on Yuki-chan.
